---
title: "Matryoshka Doll Testing"
format: html
---

The dataset is the n = 442, p = 64 Diabetes dataset (included in this Git repo) commonly used as an example dataset for variable selection.

The Peter Hoff, *A First Course In Bayesian Statistical Methods*, has the following results on pg. 170, which is a dataset and analysis that has the added benefit of what Daniel lecutred as Gospel in Stat572:

![Hoff's results](hoff_pg_170.png)

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
load("diabetes.RData")
```

Using the LMMCMC package for S = 100,000:

```{r}
# Testing Daniel's official LMMCMC package for Matryoshka Doll
library(LMMCMC)
y <- as.data.frame(scale(diabetes$y))
md <- lm.mcmc(y, diabetes$X, model.prior = matryoshka_doll.prior(), coef.prior = hyper_g.prior(), burnin.iterations = 0, mcmc.iterations = 100000)
sum(md$postprobs.RN)
#model_weights <- exp(md$logmarg+log(md$priorprobs))
#model_weights <- model_weights/sum(model_weights) # normalize
model_weights <- md$postprobs.RN
n <- length(model_weights)
models <- lapply(1:n, function(x) md$which[[x]][-1])
marg_inc_probs <- rep(0,64)
for(loop in 1:n){
  marg_inc_probs[models[[loop]]] <- marg_inc_probs[models[[loop]]] + model_weights[loop]
}
#marg_inc_probs
#barplot(marg_inc_probs, names.arg=seq(1, 64, length=64), main="Matryoshka Doll Prior, eta = 1", xlab="regressor index", ylab="P(zj=1|y,X)")
df <- as.data.frame(marg_inc_probs)
ggplot(df, aes(x = seq(1, 64, length=64), y = marg_inc_probs)) + geom_col(fill = "#0000FF") + labs(title = expression(bold(paste("Marginal Inclusion Probability"))), subtitle = expression(paste("Matryoshka Doll Prior, ", eta, " = 1")), x = "regressor index", y = expression(paste("P(", z[j], " = 1|y, X)"))) + theme_minimal() + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 32, face = "bold"), plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 28, face = "bold"), axis.text = element_text(size = 18), axis.title.x = element_text(size = 28), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 28))
```

This is the Ordered Bell Numbers:

```{r}
#| eval: false
# ordered bell numbers
n <- 64
an <- c(1, 3)
hold <- 1
for (o_loop in 3:n) {
  
  hold <- 0
  for (i_loop in 1:(o_loop-1)) {
    
    hold <- choose(o_loop, i_loop)*an[(o_loop-i_loop)] + hold
    
  }
  hold <- hold + 1
  an <- c(an, hold)
  
}
an
rat <- matrix(, nrow=231, ncol=1, byrow=TRUE)
rat[1] <- 1
for (loop in 1:63) {
  
  rat[loop+1] <- an[loop]/an[loop+1]
  #rat[loop+1] <- rat[loop+1]*(loop+1)
  
}
for (loop in 64:(231-1)) {

  rat[loop+1] <- log(2)/(loop+1)

}
rat
```

This is the Matryoshka Doll Gibbs sampler:

```{r}
#| eval: false
# CAUTION!!!!!  This Gibb's sampler takes like 30-45 minutes to run even on a fast computer btw
# Gibbs functions
getZ <- function(f_md, f_j, f_ka, f_kb, f_x_a, f_x_b) {
  
  f_sigma_a <- try(summary(lm(y ~ -1 + f_x_a))$sigma^2, silent=TRUE)
  f_sigma_b <- try(summary(lm(y ~ -1 + f_x_b))$sigma^2, silent=TRUE)
  if (f_ka==0) { SSRa <- t(y)%*%(diag(rep(1, n)))%*%y; f_sigma_a <- mean(y^2) } else { SSRa <- t(y)%*%(diag(rep(1, n)) - (g/(g+1))*(f_x_a%*%solve(t(f_x_a)%*%f_x_a)%*%t(f_x_a)))%*%y }
  if (f_kb==0) { SSRb <- t(y)%*%(diag(rep(1, n)))%*%y; f_sigma_b <- mean(y^2) } else { SSRb <- t(y)%*%(diag(rep(1, n)) - (g/(g+1))*(f_x_b%*%solve(t(f_x_b)%*%f_x_b)%*%t(f_x_b)))%*%y }
  oj <- f_md*(1+n)^((f_kb - f_ka)/2)*(f_sigma_a/f_sigma_b)^(1/2)*((f_sigma_b + SSRb)/(f_sigma_a + SSRa))^((n+1)/2)
  return(rbinom(1, 1, oj/(1+oj)))
  
}

# initialize variables
X <- as.matrix(diabetes$X)
y <- as.matrix(diabetes$y)
y[,1] <- scale(y[,1])
z <- rep(0, 64)
n <- length(y); g <- length(y)
s <- 1000
z_s <- matrix(, nrow=s, ncol=64, byrow=TRUE)
z_s[1,] <- z
for (loop in 2:s) {
  
  for (j in 1:64) {
    
    zb <- z
    zb[j] <- 1-zb[j]
    ka <- sum(z)
    kb <- sum(zb)
    if (z[j] == 1) { md <- rat[(min(ka, kb)+1)] } else { md <- 1/rat[(min(ka, kb)+1)] }
    if (z[j] == 1) { z[j] <- getZ(md, j, ka, kb, X[,z==1], X[,zb==1]) } else { z[j] <- 1-getZ(md, j, ka, kb, X[,z==1], X[,zb==1]) }
    
  }
  z_s[loop,] <- z
  
}

results <- apply(z_s, 2, mean)
results
df <- as.data.frame(results)
ggplot(df, aes(x = seq(1, 64, length=64), y = results)) + geom_col(fill = "#0000FF") + labs(title = expression(bold(paste("Marginal Inclusion Probability"))), subtitle = expression(paste("Uniform Prior")), x = "regressor index", y = expression(paste("P(", z[j], " = 1|y, X)"))) + theme_minimal() + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 32, face = "bold"), plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 28, face = "bold"), axis.text = element_text(size = 18), axis.title.x = element_text(size = 28), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 28))
```

This is the Uniform Prior Gibbs sampler:

```{r}
#| eval: false
# CAUTION!!!!!  This Gibb's sampler takes like 30-45 minutes to run even on a fast computer btw
# Gibbs functions
getZ <- function(f_j, f_ka, f_kb, f_x_a, f_x_b) {
  
  f_sigma_a <- try(summary(lm(y ~ -1 + f_x_a))$sigma^2, silent=TRUE)
  f_sigma_b <- try(summary(lm(y ~ -1 + f_x_b))$sigma^2, silent=TRUE)
  if (f_ka==0) { SSRa <- t(y)%*%(diag(rep(1, n)))%*%y; f_sigma_a <- mean(y^2) } else { SSRa <- t(y)%*%(diag(rep(1, n)) - (g/(g+1))*(f_x_a%*%solve(t(f_x_a)%*%f_x_a)%*%t(f_x_a)))%*%y }
  if (f_kb==0) { SSRb <- t(y)%*%(diag(rep(1, n)))%*%y; f_sigma_b <- mean(y^2) } else { SSRb <- t(y)%*%(diag(rep(1, n)) - (g/(g+1))*(f_x_b%*%solve(t(f_x_b)%*%f_x_b)%*%t(f_x_b)))%*%y }
  oj <- (1+n)^((f_kb - f_ka)/2)*(f_sigma_a/f_sigma_b)^(1/2)*((f_sigma_b + SSRb)/(f_sigma_a + SSRa))^((n+1)/2)
  return(rbinom(1, 1, oj/(1+oj)))
  
}

# initialize variables
X <- as.matrix(diabetes$X)
y <- as.matrix(diabetes$y)
y[,1] <- scale(y[,1])
z <- rep(0, 64)
n <- length(y); g <- length(y)
s <- 1000
z_s <- matrix(, nrow=s, ncol=64, byrow=TRUE)
z_s[1,] <- z
for (loop in 2:s) {
  
  for (j in 1:64) {
    
    zb <- z
    zb[j] <- 1-zb[j]
    ka <- sum(z)
    kb <- sum(zb)
    if (z[j] == 1) { z[j] <- getZ(j, ka, kb, X[,z==1], X[,zb==1]) } else { z[j] <- 1-getZ(j, ka, kb, X[,z==1], X[,zb==1]) }
    
  }
  z_s[loop,] <- z
  
}

results <- apply(z_s, 2, mean)
results
df <- as.data.frame(results)
ggplot(df, aes(x = seq(1, 64, length=64), y = results)) + geom_col(fill = "#0000FF") + labs(title = expression(bold(paste("Marginal Inclusion Probability"))), subtitle = expression(paste("Uniform Prior")), x = "regressor index", y = expression(paste("P(", z[j], " = 1|y, X)"))) + theme_minimal() + theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 32, face = "bold"), plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 28, face = "bold"), axis.text = element_text(size = 18), axis.title.x = element_text(size = 28), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 28))
```


This section is simple Backwards Selection:

```{r}
y <- as.data.frame(scale(diabetes$y))
model_back_full <- lm(y ~ diabetes$X)
summary(model_back_full)
model_back_step1 <- lm(y ~ diabetes$X[,"sex"] + diabetes$X[,"bmi"] + diabetes$X[,"map"] + diabetes$X[, "age:sex"])
summary(model_back_step1)
model_back_step2 <- lm(y ~ diabetes$X[,"bmi"] + diabetes$X[,"map"] + diabetes$X[, "age:sex"])
summary(model_back_step2)
```

This section is a LASSO:

```{r}
y <- as.data.frame(scale(diabetes$y))
library(glmnet) # lasso
cv_lasso <- cv.glmnet(x=diabetes$X, y=y, alpha = 1, intercept=TRUE, family = "gaussian")
plot(cv_lasso)
model_lasso <- glmnet(x=diabetes$X, y=y, alpha = 1, intercept=TRUE, family = "gaussian", lambda = cv_lasso$lambda.1se)
coef(model_lasso, lambda = cv_lasso$lambda.1se)
#-log(cv_lasso$lambda.min)
#-log(cv_lasso$lambda.1se)
```
